clue.text: Stud having stump for leg

parts.note: a stump, the end left over of a cigarette or tree, is a butt
in cricket the leg side is also called the on side, so leg gives ON

explanation.surface: A farm animal kept for breeding has lost a limb and makes do with a stump.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests a peg-legged stallion, but 'Stud' is the fastener on a shirt. In cricket the leg side of the field is also called the on side.
explanation.definitionFit: A stud and the other item are both small fasteners pushed through a hole in clothing.

clue.text: Knocked out west of Hebrides in Cruel Sea

parts.note: cruel means bad

indicators.note: in tells us the out-plus-letter piece goes inside the word for the sea

parts.note: Med is short for the Mediterranean Sea
taken as written

indicators.note: in a word written left to right its western end is the first letter, so Hebrides gives its opening letter

explanation.surface: A war film about sailors left unconscious off the Scottish islands.
explanation.walkthrough: The Cruel Sea is a classic British naval war film, which the surface plays on; 'Knocked' is not unconscious but criticised. 'west of' takes the first letter of Hebrides, and 'in' puts that run inside the sea.
explanation.definitionFit: To knock someone is to criticise them, and to have spoken ill of them is the same idea in slang.

clue.text: An opinion from both sides?

indicators.note: the question asks the solver to find a word that reads the same whichever end you start from

parts.note: these definition words give the whole answer, and the answer is itself the palindrome: it reads the same from either end

explanation.surface: Asking whether a view can be seen from either camp in an argument.
explanation.walkthrough: 'from both sides' suggests a balanced view in a debate, but it means the word itself reads identically forwards and backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: A tenet is a principle or belief someone holds, close to an opinion.

clue.text: Soar above bridge having components assembled incorrectly

indicators.note: the two parts of the word for the bridge are put together in the wrong order, so one part moves to the other end

parts.note: a flyover is a bridge carrying one road over another

explanation.surface: Something flies over a bridge that was badly built from its parts.
explanation.walkthrough: Take FLYOVER and put its two halves the other way round: FLY moves to the end behind OVER.
explanation.definitionFit: To fly over something is to soar above it in the air.

clue.text: Make fast, hard calculation about increase

indicators.note: about here means turned round, so the whole run of pieces is read backwards

parts.note: to moor a boat is to make it fast with ropes
H is the abbreviation for hard, as on pencils
a sum is a calculation

explanation.surface: Instructions for a quick, tough piece of arithmetic involving growth.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Make fast' wants to be the definition; it is wordplay, and the definition is 'increase' at the far end. 'about' turns the whole three-piece run round, not just one piece.
explanation.definitionFit: To spring up and grow very rapidly is to multiply in the manner of fungi overnight, a sudden rise.

clue.text: Dung-fly regularly landing on one's fruit

definitions.note: fruit here is collective, standing for several of the citrus fruits

indicators.note: regularly means taking every other letter of the hyphenated word, starting with the second

parts.note: one is I, and the 's adds S

explanation.surface: A dung-fly keeps settling on somebody's fruit.
explanation.walkthrough: Every second letter of DUNG-FLY gives UGL, then 'one's' is I + S.
explanation.definitionFit: An ugli is a Jamaican citrus hybrid of grapefruit and tangerine, so several are fruit.

clue.text: Informed about vitamin in part of body

parts.note: to be hip to something is to be informed about it
B1 is a vitamin (thiamine); read the numeral as a word, B ONE

explanation.surface: Someone knowledgeable about a vitamin found in a part of the body.
explanation.walkthrough: The vitamin is B1, written with the numeral spelt out as the word ONE.
explanation.definitionFit: The pelvic bone at the side of the hip is a part of the skeleton.

clue.text: Liberal welcomed in new societal swing

indicators.note: welcomed in means the abbreviation is taken inside the rearranged word
new means the letters of the following word are made into a fresh arrangement

explanation.surface: A Liberal politician is welcomed in a social change of direction.
explanation.walkthrough: 'new' rearranges SOCIETAL to OSCIATE, and 'welcomed in' puts L inside it, giving OSCILLATE.
explanation.definitionFit: To move back and forth regularly, like a pendulum, is to swing.

clue.text: Old Virginia county

annotationWithheld.why: Old Virginia county (4) for MAYO: Mayo is an Irish county; no parse makes MAYO from 'Old Virginia', and searching the exact clue found nothing, so a word may be misread or missing

clue.text: Wrap head of poorly bird sitting under tree

indicators.note: in a down answer the bird's letters come below the tree's
head of means the opening letter of the next word

parts.note: the ash is a tree
mina is a variant spelling of myna, the starling-like bird

explanation.surface: A sick bird perches beneath a tree, its head wrapped up.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'sitting under' puts MINA below ASH. Mina is a variant spelling of myna.
explanation.definitionFit: A pashmina is a fine cashmere shawl, which is worn as a wrap.

clue.text: Room for old-timers, say?

parts.note: old-timers seems to mean elderly people, but read as old-time dances it describes a hall where such dances are held

explanation.surface: Asking where elderly folk might be housed.
explanation.walkthrough: Old-time dancing is a ballroom style; the room is for old-time dances, not old people.
explanation.definitionFit: A large room hired out for dancing would host waltzes and other old-time steps.

clue.text: Still fussy in report

indicators.note: in report means as spoken, so the word for fussy is heard rather than spelt

parts.note: fussy means picky

explanation.surface: Someone remains fussy when writing a report.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Still' looks like an adverb, but it is a still photograph. 'in report' signals that PICKY is heard, giving PICCY.
explanation.definitionFit: A piccy is informal British slang for a picture, and a still is a single photograph.

clue.text: Delightful alien

explanation.surface: A charming visitor from another planet.
explanation.definitionFit: Something wonderful is called superb in this idiom; something from another planet is literally extraterrestrial.

clue.text: Perverse heartless thief's off, having got on the outside

indicators.note: on the outside means the word for got goes round the rearranged letters

parts.note: to land something, such as a job or a fish, is to get it

indicators.note: off means the remaining letters go wrong and are rearranged
heartless means the middle letter of the five-letter word is dropped

parts.note: thief is, with the 's read as is

explanation.surface: A thief with no heart makes off, having climbed out onto the exterior.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heartless' removes the middle I, 'off' rearranges what is left of the thief, and 'on the outside' wraps the word for got around it. The 's of thief's is read as 'is'.
explanation.definitionFit: Left-handed can mean awkward, ambiguous or underhand, as in a backhanded compliment, so contrary.

clue.text: Girl wandering topless catches cold

indicators.note: catches means the shortened word takes the next letter inside it
topless means the first letter is taken off

parts.note: a stray is wandering
C is the abbreviation for cold, as on taps

explanation.surface: A girl roaming about without a top on catches a chill.
explanation.walkthrough: 'topless' takes S from STRAY to leave TRAY, which 'catches' C.
explanation.definitionFit: Tracy is a girl's name, so it stands for any girl.

clue.text: Where you'd be secure in a new job, pocketing silver

indicators.note: pocketing means the run of pieces takes the next one inside it

parts.note: a chore is a job
Ag is the chemical symbol for silver

explanation.surface: Feeling safe in a fresh job that pays you in silver.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Where you'd be secure' describes a harbour berth for ships, not job security. 'pocketing' places the silver near the end, just before the last letter of the job.
explanation.definitionFit: A ship that has dropped its hook in a sheltered harbour is held safe there.

clue.text: Damn repeat I'm about to get scrapped

indicators.note: something scrapped is broken up, so these letters are broken up and reassembled

parts.note: C, short for circa, means about

explanation.surface: Cursing because a repeat broadcast I enjoy is about to be dropped.
explanation.walkthrough: REPEAT, IM and C are rearranged together.
explanation.definitionFit: To imprecate is to call down a curse, which is what damning someone does.

clue.text: Petty officer fed by English cook that's served up old game

indicators.note: fed by means the abbreviation for the officer takes the following pieces into its middle
in a down clue served up means the word is written bottom to top

parts.note: to bake is to cook

explanation.surface: A naval officer is given food by an English cook who serves an old-fashioned dish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'served up' turns the cook upward in a down answer, 'fed by' puts that inside the officer after English, and 'old' adds a final O.
explanation.definitionFit: Peekaboo is a hiding-and-revealing play used to amuse babies.

clue.text: Support points about how old we are?

parts.note: E and N are compass points, east and north
C, short for circa, means about
how old we are is our age

explanation.surface: Backing directions on the subject of our age.
explanation.walkthrough: E and N are two compass points; C is circa.
explanation.definitionFit: To support someone with words is to give them heart and spur them on.

clue.text: Lets go of perch, say

parts.note: perch suggests a bird leaving its roost, but the perch is a fish released from an angler's line

explanation.surface: A bird leaves its roost.
explanation.walkthrough: 'perch' looks like a bird's roost; it is a freshwater fish, freed from the line by an angler.
explanation.definitionFit: An angler releasing a caught fish frees it from the barb on the line.

clue.text: Still I run into trap

indicators.note: into means the abbreviation goes inside the word for trap

parts.note: a net is a trap
R is the cricket abbreviation for run

explanation.surface: Someone is still stuck in a snare after running into it.
explanation.walkthrough: I, then NET with R put inside by 'into'.
explanation.definitionFit: Something inert has no power to move, so it stays motionless.

clue.text: Arches found in a pair of platforms

parts.note: found in gives the word in
a pair of steps is a stepladder, a set of small platforms to stand on

explanation.surface: Arches discovered in a pair of raised platforms.
explanation.walkthrough: A 'pair of steps' is an old name for a stepladder, whose treads are small platforms; 'Arches' are those of the feet.
explanation.definitionFit: The raised curved middle part of each foot is its arch.

clue.text: Put a couple of horses out in South African Republic, or old homeland there?

indicators.note: in means the rearranged letters go inside the country's name

parts.note: Botswana is a republic in southern Africa

indicators.note: out means these letters are disordered

parts.note: taken as written
H is slang for heroin, called horse, so two of them is HH

explanation.surface: Moving two horses outside in a southern African country.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' rearranges the letters and 'in' places them after the first two letters of the country. Bophuthatswana was one of apartheid South Africa's nominally independent black homelands.
explanation.definitionFit: Bophuthatswana was a bantustan set up for the Tswana people under apartheid.

clue.text: Vegetable found in pipe run

parts.note: a tube is a pipe
R is the cricket abbreviation for run

explanation.surface: A vegetable discovered blocking a drainpipe.
explanation.definitionFit: A potato is a tuber, the swollen underground stem of a plant eaten as a vegetable.

clue.text: Inward psyche turned up in examination

indicators.note: in a down clue turned up means the hidden letters read from bottom to top
in means the letters sit inside the single word that follows

explanation.surface: A deep self-analysis comes out in a test.
explanation.walkthrough: Inside examination sits AMINA; 'turned up' reverses it.
explanation.definitionFit: In Jungian theory the anima is the inner self or soul, the inward personality.

clue.text: Left stuck in empty gorge

indicators.note: stuck in means the abbreviation goes inside the word for empty

parts.note: to gut a fish is to empty it

explanation.surface: Someone abandoned and trapped in a barren ravine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gorge' looks like a ravine but is the verb, to stuff oneself; 'empty' is the verb gut.
explanation.definitionFit: To glut oneself is to eat to excess, the same as gorging.

clue.text: Plain score draw about to see off English

indicators.note: to see off means to get rid of the following letter
about means the phrase is turned round

parts.note: a one-all score is a score draw in football

explanation.surface: A dull football match ends level, about to beat an English side.
explanation.walkthrough: A score draw is a drawn football match with goals, such as one-all. 'about' turns ONEALL into LLAENO; 'to see off' removes E.
explanation.definitionFit: A llano is a grassy treeless plain of South America.

clue.text: British capital one invested in macho man's plant

parts.note: Rome is the capital of Italy

indicators.note: invested in means put inside the word for the macho man

parts.note: a lad is a laddish, macho young man
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: British money put into a he-man's factory.
explanation.walkthrough: 'plant' looks like a factory, but here it is a living plant; 'invested in' puts I inside LAD.
explanation.definitionFit: A bromeliad is a member of the pineapple family, many grown as houseplants.

clue.text: Present almost certain to achieve value

indicators.note: almost means the last letter is left off

parts.note: a treat is a present
sure means certain

explanation.surface: A gift that is nearly guaranteed to be worth something.
explanation.walkthrough: 'almost' cuts the final T from TREAT; 'value' is a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To treasure something is to prize or cherish it highly.

clue.text: Man is one in reality but not in Meditation

definitions.text: Man is one in reality but not in Meditation

parts.words: Man is one in reality but not in Meditation
parts.note: the Isle of Man is a piece of land in the sea, yet John Donne's Meditation XVII says no man is such a thing

explanation.surface: A philosophical point on what a man is, in life versus in contemplation.
explanation.walkthrough: Capital 'Meditation' points to John Donne's Meditation XVII, 'No man is an island'; Man is also the Isle of Man in the Irish Sea.
explanation.definitionFit: The Isle of Man is land surrounded by sea, unlike the men in Donne's famous line.
